paragraphs: Here's what this passage teaches, friend. God doesn't leave it up to opinion who He has chosen. Twelve plain staffs go in, and only one comes out with buds, blossoms and almonds (Numbers 17:8). That staff was Aaron's, and nobody could say Moses made it up, because it grew overnight with no help from anybody.

Now look at who the sign was for. God calls it "a sign for the rebellious" and says the grumbling was against Him (Numbers 17:10). That tells me grumbling at the people God has put in place isn't a small thing in His eyes. And listen to why He gives the sign: "so that you may put an end to their grumbling against Me, lest they die." I think that's a God who is trying to stop trouble before it lands, and He does it with a stick that grew almonds.

So what do you do with that, baker? When you catch yourself grumbling, ask whose plan you're really complaining about. And when God shows you something clear, don't fight it, because I fought the drawer for years and the drawer never budged. The people end the passage crying, "Are we all going to perish?" (Numbers 17:13). That question is still hanging, and the story isn't over.
